summary: One declarative span request is fully planned before writes: product-grid prices and apportioned sizes, deterministic UUID5 client_order_id values, flat root linkage, and per-rung reveal/anchor materialization. The bridge acquires every rung action lock in deterministic order, verifies all existing deterministic IDs and missing-root profitability before the first write, then delegates missing rungs to the canonical single-order manager path. Runtime failure stops later rungs and returns explicit partial state; an identical retry accepts matching durable rows and creates only missing rungs.

A span is not one database transaction. Each rung uses the canonical manager creation transaction, so an unpredictable persistence failure can leave earlier rungs durable. Deterministic IDs, stop-on-first-failure results, and matching-row retry make that partial state explicit and resumable; automatic rollback or cancellation is intentionally absent.

guardrails: Use client_order_id for every deterministic rung and root link.
Keep all child parent_order_id values linked directly to rung zero.
Plan and normalize the complete request before the first write.
Do not describe cross-rung creation as atomic; return and resume explicit partial state.
Keep the manager single-order creation method as the only persistence path.
